newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close lower as soybeans slide.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close lower as soybeans slide.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed lower on a late collapse in soybean futures inspired by a slowdown in exports, near-ideal crop weather in South America and a bearish crop forecast from Sparks Companies CEO Carrol Brunthaver, traders said.
Soyoil was underpinned by unwinding of meal/oil spreads amid some talk about low yields of oil in this year's U.S. soybean crop, traders said.
"The talk of lower oil content may be a little supportive but not enough to change anyone's ideas much," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Cermak and others said the oil/meal spread was going through a seasonal adjustment plus there was some bullish input to soyoil on signals commercials were getting long soyoil, the traders said.
Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report showed as of December 3 commercials were long soyoil roughly 42,506 lots and short 41,091 lots.
Soyoil closed 0.09 cent per lb lower to 0.10 higher, with December down 0.04 at 23.13. Soymeal was $1.50 to $3.80 per ton lower, with December down $2.90 at $230.30.
The commercial longs increased by roughly 2,562 lots from the previous reporting period and the commercial shorts decreased by roughly 3,442 lots.
Soymeal was pressured by the recent strong soybean crush pace and the unwinding of the meal/oil spreads.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 21,000 contracts, above the 18,590 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 19,000 contracts, below the 35,081 traded Friday.
